result.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
result.comment: 23 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to ACL Rolling Review (October 2026)
result.summary: Self-evolving agents accumulate experience from task streams, but existing frameworks typically rely on fixed pipelines to retrieve and utilize this experience, neglecting when and how to deploy it. We introduce Online Meta-Control of Experience (OMCE), a framework that updates experience memory and learns a meta-control policy from task feedback during test-time adaptation. OMCE employs a lightweight contextual-bandit meta-controller that uses compact retrieval signals to select among four cognitive actions: DIRECT, EPISODE, GUIDE, and DISTILL. This routing mechanism operationalizes three coupled decisions: whether to invoke experience, which memory format to utilize, and when to consolidate new guidance. OMCE evolves online, leveraging task feedback to update the memory bank and refine the routing policy via contextual bandit updates. Experiments on four online adaptation benchmarks across four backbones show that OMCE improves first-attempt success by up to 20.5 percentage points over the strongest compared baseline, while reducing per-task token use by a factor of 5.7 to 62.5 relative to ACE with GPT-5.2. Controlled ablations further support the benefits of learned routing and continued routing policy adaptation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OMCE，在测试时用轻量 contextual bandit 元控制器依据检索信号在 DIRECT、EPISODE、GUIDE、DISTILL 四种认知动作间路由，并据任务反馈在线更新经验记忆与路由策略，在多个在线适应基准上提升首次成功率并大幅降低 token 消耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 其元控制器以紧凑信号学习「何时调用经验、用哪种记忆格式」，可能为 LVR 中是否检索视觉证据、何时合并与停止的决策策略提供可核查的借鉴线索，但论文本身不涉及视觉输入或 latent 状态。
